sections.title: Humanitarian and parole programs, Biden period
notes: Sums for FY2021–FY2024 (FY2021 includes about 3.7 months under Trump; FY2025 is not yet published):
Refugee arrivals: 197,080.
Asylum grants: 171,330 (76,910 affirmative; 94,420 defensive).
Annual trend. Refugee arrivals rose from 11,450 (FY2021) to 100,060 (FY2024). Asylum grants rose from 16,450 to 68,170.
Parole:
CHNV parole: about 532,000 (Oct 2022–Jan 2025).
CBP One: more than 936,500 appointments scheduled (Jan 2023–Dec 2024).
Both ended in 2025. The Supreme Court allowed the CHNV terminations (May 30, 2025).
DACA: 436,350 active recipients (Jun 30, 2026).
Not reported as annual series: TPS, OAW, U4U, border parole, and I-765 approvals by category. USCIS publishes I-765 data quarterly only, and summing quarters is prohibited.
No amnesty law has been enacted since IRCA (1986).

sections.title: Judicial Watch voter-roll cases: court records vs. claims
notes: LA County (JW v. Logan, C.D. Cal. 2:17-cv-08948, settled Jan 2019).
The settlement covers about 1,565,000 inactive registrations and requires NVRA notices, with cancellation of non-responders who miss the required federal elections.
Judicial Watch's headline said "remove 1.5 million."
Kentucky (JW v. Grimes, E.D. Ky. 3:17-cv-94): consent judgment entered Jul 3, 2018 requiring a list-maintenance program.
Colorado (JW v. Griswold, D. Colo. 20-cv-02992).
Settled Mar 2023: annual data reporting through 2028, dismissal without prejudice, no admission of liability.
The court's Feb 27, 2024 order records that the Secretary's discovery figure of 306,303 8(d)(1)(B) removals was erroneous. Judicial Watch said the correct figure was 101,607.
EAVS 2022 shows 161,607 Colorado removals for failure to respond to confirmation notices.
Related Supreme Court case. Husted v. A. Philip Randolph Institute (2018) upheld Ohio's supplemental process; it was not a Judicial Watch case.

voters-23.title: Population and citizenship
lines: Citizens. ACS counts 277.6M U.S. citizens in 2006 and 315.7M in 2024. Noncitizens were 21.8M in 2006, 20.2M in the 2020 experimental estimate (not comparable) and 24.4M in 2024.
Comparability. The 2005 figures cover households only. The 2020 figures are experimental and have no CVAP table. The 2025 ACS has not been released.

voters-24.title: Voter registration
lines: EAVS registrations (state administrative counts, including inactive records) were 172.8M (2006), 189.8M (2008), 214.1M (2016), 228.0M (2020), 226.3M (2022) and 234.5M (2024).

Documented reasons for changes. EAC documents one: the 2004→2006 decline, which it attributes to HAVA statewide databases removing duplicates. The 2014 figure is not comparable because some states reported active voters only. For other cycles, the sources pulled give no cause.
CPS self-reported registration of citizens was 135.8M (2006) and 173.9M (2024), in thousands in the source. EAVS and CPS measure different things (see the Discrepancies sheet).

Native-born vs naturalized. There is no administrative count of registrants by native-born vs naturalized status. CPS self-reports show naturalized-citizen registrants of 7.6M (2006) and 15.9M (2024).
more: Main reasons: moved; died; failed to respond to an NVRA notice and did not vote in two federal elections.
The 2024 errata revised several reason counts.
Registration method. Motor-vehicle offices and AVR supply the largest share. In 2024 there were 31.8M MVA and 26.1M AVR transactions out of 103.5M.

voters-25.title: Naturalization
lines: FY2007 and FY2008. Applications jumped to 1.38M in FY2007, ahead of the July 2007 fee increase and the 2008 election. Persons naturalized peaked at 1,046,540 in FY2008.
FY2020. Naturalizations dipped to 628,250 during COVID-19 office closures.
FY2022. They reached 969,380 during backlog reduction.

voters-72.title: Kamala Harris · voter rolls
lines: What was said: Trump is purging the voter rolls (the claim as it circulated; her transcribed words were "They are cheating by purging voter rolls").
Said by Kamala Harris (Detroit NAACP forum, Sep 22, 2026; she said "they," not Trump)
Quote: see the grey box below (secondary transcriptions).

What the record shows: No federal agency has removed anyone from a state roll; states keep the rolls under the NVRA. The administration has pressed states through two executive orders, DOJ suits for voter lists (22+ dismissed), and DHS SAVE bulk checks (vacated in June 2026; stay pending). Some states cancelled registrations using SAVE data; in Texas, 578 of 2,724 people flagged were later shown to be citizens and ordered reinstated if removed.
Context Her advice to check registration status is not a factual claim and is not rated.
voters-72.label: Rated misleading

voters-73.title: "30,000 illegal aliens registered" (TV report, about Sep 23, 2026)
lines: What was said: 30,000 illegal aliens are registered to vote.
Said by A television report (segment not identified)
The specific broadcast was not identified.

What the record shows: The figure traces to a Reuters investigation (Sep 23, 2026): states "may have added more than 30,000 self-declared noncitizens" to rolls since 2000, across 12 states, because of DMV software glitches and clerical errors. It does not say they were in the country illegally (the group includes lawful permanent residents), and Reuters could not determine how many voted. Primary records it relied on include New Jersey (about 6,600) and Iowa (277; 35 ballots).
Context Cumulative over 26 years in 12 states, any immigration status, and nothing about voting.
voters-73.label: Rated misleading

voters-74.title: Colorado Secretary of State registration postcards reached deceased people and noncitizens (Sept 2020)
lines: The mailing is confirmed by the Secretary of State's own letter; that it reached deceased people and noncitizens is reported by CBS4 and Breitbart, not by an official record.

What was sent (official): a mailing inviting potentially eligible but unregistered Coloradans to register, required at least once every two years under the state's contract with the Electronic Registration Information Center (ERIC). Secretaries Gessler (2012, 2014) and Williams (2016, 2018) sent the same mailing.

How the list was built (official): ERIC starts from all Coloradans with a driver's license, removes those already registered, and screens out people on state or federal deceased lists, in group homes, incarcerated for a felony, or who showed a noncitizen credential. The list is not a public record.
more: What was reported: CBS4 found about a dozen cards that reached deceased people and noncitizens. The office said the card is not a ballot, lists the voting qualifications in bold, and that mailings are not always 100% correct.
Official record: Secretary of State letter to the Legislative Audit Committee, Dec 14, 2020 (Q6–Q10) · Lead source: Breitbart, Sep 27, 2020 · CBS4 follow-up, Sep 27, 2020

The 2022 postcards (as reported by AP and AFP from the Secretary of State's statements). On Sep 27, 2022 her office mailed ERIC-required registration-information postcards (not forms or ballots) to about 30,000 noncitizens; a later count was 31,093. The cause was a Department of Revenue list that lacked the formatting needed to screen out noncitizen license holders. The office said the online system rejects noncitizen licenses and SSNs and that it knew of no recipient who registered. AP via CBS Colorado AFP Fact Check Fox News, Oct 10, 2022 (no Secretary of State release on the 2022 mailing was found on coloradosos.gov)
voters-74.label: Not yet verified

sources.label: Secretary of State letter to the Legislative Audit Committee, Dec 14, 2020 (Q6–Q10)

voters-75.title: Colorado Secretary of State website posted partial voting-equipment passwords (June–Oct 2024)
lines: The office's own releases, an outside investigation, the Denver District Attorney and a court ruling confirm it.

What was posted: a spreadsheet on the Department's website with a hidden tab holding partial BIOS passwords (one of two passwords) for some voting-system components. A former staff member created it; storing passwords this way broke Department policy.

How long and how many: posted June 21, 2024 and taken down Oct 24, 2024, when a voting-machine vendor told the office; 34 of 64 counties affected. County clerks were told Oct 29; all affected active equipment had new passwords by Oct 31, with no settings found changed.
more: What the office said, and the outcome: Secretary Griswold: “I am regretful for this error.” The outside investigation (Baird Quinn LLC, Dec 9, 2024) found the passwords were posted “mistakenly, unknowingly and unintentionally” and made seven recommendations, which the office committed to adopt. The Denver DA found no criminal violation (published “in error and not ‘knowingly’”). On Nov 5, 2024 a Denver District Court judge denied a petition over it (Libertarian Party v. Griswold), finding no evidence of compromised components.

Official records: SOS statement, Oct 29, 2024 SOS update, Nov 4, 2024 Court ruling (SOS release), Nov 5, 2024 Baird Quinn report (SOS release), Dec 9, 2024 Denver DA finding (SOS release), Dec 20, 2024
voters-75.label: Verified (official record)
